name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,115

clue.text: Nuts about large island’s birds

indicators.note: the nuts are placed around something else, so they surround the other letters

blocks.note: pecans are a kind of nut
L is the standard abbreviation for large
I is the abbreviation for island; the possessive just smooths the surface

explanation.surface: Some nuts lying around a big island turn out to belong to its birds.
explanation.walkthrough: L and I sit inside PECANS to give PE-LI-CANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelicans are large waterbirds with a throat pouch, so they are examples of birds.

clue.text: Nasty smell starts to put off nice guests

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of these four words

explanation.surface: A nasty smell begins to drive away polite visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: PONG is everyday British slang for a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a pong is an unpleasant odour, a stink.

clue.text: Wrinkle on new flax cloth

blocks.note: a line on the face is a wrinkle
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A crease appears on freshly made flaxen fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is the fabric woven from fibres of the flax plant.

clue.text: Actor playing Chandler’s ace

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are being played about with and rearranged

blocks.note: every letter of these two words, the possessive S included

explanation.surface: An actor appears in the role of Raymond Chandler's star detective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' reads like an actor taking a part; it is the signal to rearrange the letters of Chandler's ace into CHARLES DANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Dance is an English film and television actor, known for Game of Thrones.

clue.text: Spiritual movement reduced net salary

indicators.note: something reduced is cut short, so the word that follows loses its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
a wage is a regular payment for work

explanation.surface: Someone complains that their take-home pay has been cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduced' looks like it describes the salary, but it trims only the word net.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Age movement is a loose Western spiritual trend embracing alternative beliefs and holistic practices.

clue.text: Corvid, rook, hidden by bovine

indicators.note: a thing hidden by another is enclosed within it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a cow is a bovine animal
R is the chess notation for a rook

explanation.surface: A rook, one of the crow family, is tucked out of sight behind a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook' looks like a second bird beside the definition, but here it is the chess piece, R, placed inside COW.
explanation.definitionFit: Corvids are the bird family including ravens, jackdaws and magpies, and the carrion bird in question is its namesake member.

clue.text: More hasty invader punched by Penny

indicators.note: being punched by something means it is driven into you, so one piece is inserted in the other

blocks.note: a raider is an attacker who invades
P is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: An attacker gets thumped by a woman called Penny and flees faster.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid means quick, and its comparative form describes something swifter or done in greater haste.

clue.text: What to wear when fighting female prison officer?

blocks.note: first meaning, read cryptically: clothing for battle
second meaning: a woman warder in a jail

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a playful reading of the word split as WAR DRESS, the outfit for combat.
explanation.definitionFit: A wardress is the old-fashioned term for a woman who guards prisoners, the feminine form of warder.

clue.text: Perhaps Beijing increases profits

blocks.note: Beijing is an example of a capital city, as 'perhaps' signals
gains are increases

explanation.surface: China's capital boosts its earnings.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital gains are the profits made when assets such as shares or property are sold for more than they cost.

clue.text: Special offer from Japan in Japanese

definitions.note: a noun here: a special operative

indicators.note: what is offered from inside a phrase is drawn out of its run of letters

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A shop advertises a bargain imported from Japan, labelled in Japanese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special offer' reads as a bargain, but 'Special' alone is the definition and 'offer from' points into the letters of Japan in Japanese.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninja is a covert Japanese agent trained in espionage, like a special forces operative.

clue.text: Maybe Eminem picked up dust jacket?

indicators.note: picking something up can mean hearing it, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: Eminem is a well-known example of a hip-hop performer

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if the rapper Eminem grabbed a dusty coat.
explanation.walkthrough: The silent W means the hip-hop artist and the cover sound identical.
explanation.definitionFit: A dust jacket is the removable paper cover around a hardback book, a protective covering of that kind.

clue.text: Endanger girl waving around power tool

indicators.note: something waving around is flailing about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: every letter of these two words

explanation.surface: Swinging a dangerous tool about puts a young woman at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle grinder is a handheld electric tool with a spinning disc for cutting and polishing metal.

clue.text: Son fell and took clothes off

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
to trip is to stumble and fall

explanation.surface: A boy took a tumble and then got undressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip is to undress, so the past tense means removed one's garments.

clue.text: Most uninspiring test cases in the morning

indicators.note: used as a verb, to case is to enclose, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: taken as written
AM marks times before noon

explanation.surface: The dullest of the trial runs were held before noon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test cases' reads as a single noun phrase; here 'cases' is a verb meaning encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: Tame can mean dull or lacking excitement, so its superlative means the least exciting of all.

clue.text: Early showing from friend drinking at home with European

indicators.note: a drinker takes something into themselves, so the friend swallows the next piece

blocks.note: a mate is a friend
someone at home is in
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A pal having a drink at home with a European guest watches an afternoon film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At home' is a single unit meaning in, not two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A matinee is an afternoon performance of a play or film, earlier than the main evening screening.

clue.text: Piles of stones in Australian city

blocks.note: first meaning: heaped stones used as landmarks
second meaning: a city in tropical Queensland

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one picture of rock heaps in a city, but splits into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairns are mounds of rocks built as markers on hills, and Cairns is also a Queensland coastal city near the Great Barrier Reef.

clue.text: All one’s possessions in large car

blocks.note: first meaning: everything a person owns, especially at death
second meaning: a long car with a load space behind the rear seats

explanation.walkthrough: An estate car is the British name for what North Americans call a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's estate is the total property they own, and an estate car is a roomy family vehicle with a tailgate.

clue.text: Unwilling to compromise about training nets

indicators.note: about can mean scattered here and there, so the letters are moved into a different order

blocks.note: every letter of these two words

explanation.surface: A stubborn cricketer refuses to budge in an argument over the practice nets.
explanation.walkthrough: Practice nets are the netted enclosures where cricketers train.
explanation.definitionFit: Intransigent describes someone who stubbornly refuses to change their views or agree.

clue.text: Sound of one cutting bouquet

indicators.note: something cutting into another thing goes inside it

blocks.note: a wine's nose is its bouquet, its aroma
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A florist hears a sound as one snips a bunch of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouquet' suggests flowers, but here it is the scent of wine, NOSE, with I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise is any audible sound, especially a loud or unwanted one.

clue.text: Muslim ruler, am I right?

blocks.note: taken as written; that the letters also run straight through 'am I right' is a coincidence of the charade, not a hidden-word signal
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they have correctly named an Islamic leader.
explanation.definitionFit: An amir, also spelt emir, is a title for a commander or prince in Muslim countries.

clue.text: Criticise wonderful American cure-all

blocks.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
ace is slang for excellent
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a marvellous American miracle remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a supposed remedy for every illness or problem.

clue.text: Expression of fool scratching backside with enthusiasm, ultimately

indicators.note: scratching out the backside means rubbing off the rear end, so the final letter goes
ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter of the phrase is kept

blocks.note: an idiot is a fool
the closing letter of the final word

explanation.surface: A clown eagerly scratches his bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: IDIOT loses its T to give IDIO, then M is added.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a fixed phrase or turn of speech whose meaning is not literal.

clue.text: Edit changes for regime

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters are altered in their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An editor revises a document to suit the government in power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regime' suggests a government, but here it is a planned eating plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet is a prescribed eating plan, a regime of food followed for health or weight loss.

clue.text: Chaps use foul language in section of department store

blocks.note: chaps are men
to swear is to curse

explanation.surface: Some blokes curse while shopping in a big store.
explanation.definitionFit: Menswear is the department selling clothing for males, one area of a large shop.
